subject.title: Matrix DM session-key lowercasing collides case-distinct MXIDs, sharing one peer's DM transcript with another under per-peer scope

question: Should the security fix enroll only Matrix direct peers now, or also enroll Signal direct peers after proving Signal direct IDs are case-sensitive opaque principals?
rationale: The Matrix source path and documented DM isolation contract are clear, but broadening the shared registry to Signal direct changes a security-sensitive session-key boundary without the same direct-ID contract proof in this review.

options.title: Fix Matrix direct first
options.body: Preserve Matrix direct MXID case now and leave Signal direct unchanged until its direct-ID contract is proven with focused tests.

options.title: Enroll Matrix and Signal direct
options.body: Preserve both Matrix and Signal direct IDs in the registry, but require direct-ID contract proof and regressions for both channels before merge.

options.title: Wait for live homeserver proof
options.body: Defer implementation until a permissive Matrix homeserver demonstrates the full inbound-to-transcript-load leak, trading speed for stronger runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Fix Matrix direct first
recommendation.body: Preserve Matrix direct MXID case now and leave Signal direct unchanged until its direct-ID contract is proven with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and co-authored the prior Matrix opaque-ID session-key safety work and are the strongest available routing owner for a security-boundary decision.
